text:
Hendrix Lapierre has found a home in Pittsburgh's bottom six, and the numbers say he has made more of it than you might think. Eight points in 17 games at about 12 minutes a night works out to 2.32 points per 60 minutes, above the league average for a forward and well ahead of what he managed in Washington, where the Capitals drafted him 22nd overall in 2020.

The catch is how he got there. Three goals on 17 shots is a 17.6% shooting rate, against a range of roughly 10% to 15% we'd expect for him, and his last ten games produced three points. Our numbers expect him to settle around 31 points over a full season.

What makes him interesting is the passing. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 22% of his setups crossing the royal road last season, against 7% for a typical forward: the cross-ice pass that drags a goalie side to side. He scored on Juuse Saros in Nashville on Saturday, his first goal in ten games. On a Penguins team that has lost a lot lately, a smart passer on the third line is useful, even if the shooting cools.
